Melanie — great questions. Short answers inline, then an updated checklist below.

1) Regression set: we used a 250-prompt subset representative of your taxonomy (intent detection + extraction + short summarization). We can run the identical suite against your anonymized data; please share the bundle or a secure access link and we’ll schedule the run. (See related link to Drive in the metadata.)
2) Latency SLO: the 95th <= 350ms target assumes steady-state traffic with 512-token context and continuous batching. For burst spikes that exceed our configured queue depth we’ll set a 99th percentile guardrail at 700ms and a fallback policy to the smaller-capacity variant (quantized) to protect overall availability. We’ll document the exact queue depth and batch size in the MAP worksheet.
3) Cost: attached is a quick quote (redwood_quote_0426.pdf) — pilot run estimate and committed-month estimate (includes reserved capacity discount). Procurement: the pilot is low-cost and can be paid on a short-term card or P.O.

Updated acceptance checklist (proposal):
- Kickoff + connectivity (day 0): API keys, VPC peering / IP allowlist verified, authentication test pass
- Week 1: functional smoke tests, integration tests against sample data, end-to-end latency baseline run
- Week 2: regression run with customer bundle, production-like traffic simulation (20 qps sustained, 1k concurrent sessions), quality metrics computed and reviewed
- Exit gates (to move to committed):
  - Quality: concordance >= 90% (primary), no critical model failures on the regression set
  - Performance: 95th latency <= 350ms; 99th <= 700ms during simulated bursts
  - Reliability: no more than 2 P1 incidents during pilot period
  - Security: signed NDA in place, SOC2 questionnaire returned with no high-risk items, KMS integration verified

If internal team agrees, I’ll ask Lauren to finalize the smoke/regression test definitions and Hannah to own coordination for procurement/security artifacts.

Best,

Thanks for the draft, Sergio — I expanded the acceptance tests and added concrete measurement steps so both teams have deterministic pass/fail signals. Highlights:

Acceptance test catalog (excerpts):
- Smoke: auth + basic prompt -> expected intent labels returned; pass if auth succeeds and 95% of sample prompts return correctly formatted JSON
- Regression: run 250-prompt bundle x3 seeds; compute median concordance and interquartile spread; pass if median >= 92% and lower quartile >= 88%
- Hallucination check: sample 200 outputs with human review on edge cases; pass if hallucination rate < 2%
- Load: run load test ramping to 25 qps for 10 minutes; monitor queue depth and tail latency; pass if 95th <= 350ms and error rate < 0.5%
- Failover: simulate an availability zone loss in staging; pass if <1% request loss and automatic routing to fallback model occurs within 20s

Signoff parties and cadence:
- Product (Elara): Melanie — quality signoff after regression review
- Security: Tom — SOC2 checklist + KMS verification
- Redwood Ops: Ben — infrastructure and runbook verification
- Sales: Sergio — commercial approval and go/no-go call

I attached a short SLO examples doc (slo_examples.pdf) that maps telemetry metrics to dashboard widgets we’ll share during the pilot. I’ll also export the regression bundle instructions into the MAP worksheet.
